25503: In Highcharts, a polygon chart is a Cartesian chart that uses the polygon series type to draw a filled, freeform shape through a list of [x, y] points. It is useful for showing a target range or region next to observed data points, and is often combined with a scatter series. This post walks through creating one in four steps: load the scripts, add a container, style it, and initialize the chart.
25112: Highcharts® Stock lets you build interactive stock charts in JavaScript, from simple line charts of daily prices to candlestick charts with a volume pane, live-updating series, multi-series comparisons, depth charts and a Stock Tools GUI. This post walks through seven live demos, each with a link to its code.
25396: To plot latitude and longitude on a map with Highcharts® Maps, load a base map in GeoJSON or TopoJSON format, create a mapChart, and add a mappoint series whose data points have lat and lon properties. This tutorial builds an interactive map of nine UK cities with tooltips, zoom and pan, and shares best-practice tips along the way.
25266: Visualizing climate data reveals patterns, trends and anomalies that inform policy and raise public awareness. With Highcharts® Dashboards you can build an interactive climate dashboard that combines a world map, KPI gauges, a selection grid and historical trend charts. This post walks through the Highcharts climate demo, which covers cities worldwide and shows temperature in both Celsius and Fahrenheit.
27105: Chart color influences how viewers perceive, interpret and act on data, because the brain processes color before it analyzes the numbers. Choose colors that match common associations (such as red for critical and green for normal), account for cultural differences and color vision deficiency, and test them with real users. This post covers the science of color perception, cultural and accessibility considerations, and how to apply these principles in Highcharts.
26169: A box and whisker plot (boxplot) summarizes a data distribution with five values: minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, third quartile (Q3) and maximum. It shows spread, skewness and potential outliers at a glance, which makes it useful in fields from scientific research to financial analysis. In Highcharts, you create one by loading highcharts.js and highcharts-more.js and setting chart.type to 'boxplot', as this post shows step by step.
26592: IoT weather stations collect large amounts of data on temperature, wind, precipitation and more, and that data is hard to use without good visualization. This tutorial shows how to build an interactive live weather dashboard with Highcharts® Dashboards: a station map, KPI gauges, a forecast grid and a forecast chart, fed by MET Norway forecast data through a JSON data connector. It covers layout, component configuration, dark mode, responsive CSS and how to swap in your own IoT data source.
25069: Dashboards let businesses and organizations see trends, patterns and key information in one accessible place. This post shows six ready-to-explore examples built with Highcharts® Dashboards, each with a live demo: Project Management, Cloud monitoring, Personal finance, Sync of highlight cursor, Climate data and Accounting. Whether you are new to dashboards or have used them for some time, the examples offer inspiration for your own projects.
26234: A bar graph compares values across separate categories using bars with gaps between them, while a histogram shows how a continuous variable is distributed by grouping values into adjacent bins. Use a bar graph to compare categories, and a histogram to see the shape, center and spread of numeric data. This guide explains the differences, when to use each, how to read them, and how to build both with Highcharts.
25269: Real-time data visualization lets you follow financial markets, live scores or server health as they happen. Highcharts supports it in two ways: the data module with polling, which needs only configuration (a data source and a refresh interval), or API methods that update the chart programmatically from WebSockets, AJAX calls or any custom data source. This post explains both and walks through a live CSV polling example step by step.
25535: Lightning strikes about 100 times per second worldwide, and static maps cannot capture data that changes this fast. To create an interactive lightning map with Highcharts® Maps, load a base map such as Europe, add a mapbubble series for the strikes, color each strike by age with a colorAxis, and drive playback with a range input and a play/pause button. This tutorial recreates the official demo using historical strike data from frost.met.no.
26178: A network graph shows relationships as nodes (points) connected by edges (lines), revealing clusters, hierarchies and key influencers that are hard to see in a table. In Highcharts, you build one by loading highcharts.js and modules/networkgraph.js, setting chart.type to 'networkgraph', and passing from/to pairs as series data. Highcharts then positions the nodes with a force-directed layout, and users can drag them to explore relationships.
30125: Users expect the same chart experience on desktop, tablet, mobile and in print. Highcharts keeps charts consistent across all of them by using one configuration and theme for brand colors and fonts, responsive.rules breakpoints to adapt layout to screen size, and the exporting module to produce static PNG or PDF output for print. For multi-component interfaces, Highcharts Dashboards adds a Flexbox-based layout engine that repositions charts, KPI gauges and data grids across screen sizes.
31185: Healthcare data visualization turns clinical data such as vital signs, treatment outcomes, case counts and compliance metrics into charts that clinicians and administrators can act on quickly. In a clinical setting a misread trend can have serious consequences, so clarity, responsiveness and accessibility are core requirements. Highcharts supports this with real-time time-series charts, drilldown, maps, accessibility and export modules, and client-side rendering that keeps patient data inside your own environment.
25230: Highcharts is a JavaScript charting library by Highsoft that renders interactive charts in the browser, with a wide range of chart types and customization options. This post walks through six examples (column, pie, line, area, bar and scatter), explains when to use each chart type, and links to live demos with editable code.
26509: A dependency wheel is a type of chord diagram that shows directed, weighted relationships between entities arranged around a circle, which makes complex flows easier to read than in traditional charts. In Highcharts, you create one by loading highcharts.js plus the sankey.js and dependency-wheel.js modules, then adding a series of type 'dependencywheel' with data in a from, to, weight format. This post shows how, step by step.
26473: 3D charts catch attention, but they can also distort data. Use a 3D chart only when your data has three meaningful dimensions or when interactive rotation helps users explore it. Otherwise choose a 2D chart, because perspective distortion, occlusion and extra cognitive load can mislead readers. This post covers when 3D works, when it fails, and how to build 3D charts in Highcharts with the highcharts-3d.js module, including rotatable 3D scatter plots.
25292: Big data visualization turns large datasets into charts where trends, patterns and outliers are easy to spot. Highcharts handles it by combining the Boost module, which uses WebGL to offload rendering to the GPU, with interactive zooming and panning and asynchronous data loading. The demos in this post render 500,000 to 1.7 million data points, including a 1-million-point scatter chart and a 1.7-million-point AAPL stock chart.
26512: A standard deviation graph shows how far data points spread around the mean, typically as a bell curve with intervals marked in σ. A low standard deviation means values cluster near the mean; a high one means they are spread out. This guide covers its applications in statistical analysis and data science, and how to build one in Highcharts with the bellcurve series from the histogram-bellcurve module.
25434: A heat map shows the magnitude of values as color on a two-dimensional grid or a geographic area, which makes patterns and outliers easy to spot. This post walks through six interactive Highcharts examples: calendar, geo (Europe and orthographic), sales per weekday, interpolated, and large Boost-powered heat maps, each with a live demo and a link to its code.
26146: A waterfall chart shows how a starting value is increased and decreased by a series of positive and negative steps until it reaches a final total. To read one, start at the first bar, follow each floating bar up or down from where the previous bar ended, and compare the result with the subtotal and final sum bars. In Highcharts, you create one by setting chart.type to 'waterfall' and loading highcharts-more.js, as this post shows.
25418: Intraday charts show price movements within a single trading day, where a large volume of data points must stay readable. Highcharts® Stock renders them from minute-level data using area or candlestick series, with selectable time ranges, tooltips, zoom and pan. This post walks through three live demos (intraday candlestick, intraday area and intraday with breaks) and explains how each handles nights and weekends.
25625: Default chart styles can clash with your brand's design. You can customize Highcharts to match your brand by overriding the default colors, fonts and chart styles in the chart options, reusing them through themes, or moving all styling into CSS with styled mode. Pattern fills, gradients and shadows add further visual control. This guide covers each approach with live examples.
25468: Geospatial data, from sales locations to environmental change, is hard to use without the right visualization tools. Highcharts® Maps builds interactive geographic maps in JavaScript: it loads map geometry from GeoJSON or TopoJSON, or uses tiled web maps from external providers, and joins your data to map regions with the joinBy option. It supports choropleth, point and line maps with zoom, pan and tooltips, and this post helps you get started.
25312: A Pareto chart combines a bar chart and a line chart: the bars show individual categories in descending order and the line shows their cumulative percentage, so you can see which few factors cause most of the effect. It builds on the Pareto principle (the 80/20 rule), named after the Italian economist Vilfredo Pareto. In Highcharts, you build one with the pareto module and a series of type pareto, as this post shows.
25482: A choropleth map uses shades of color to represent data values across geographic regions, which makes regional patterns in demographics, public health or economics easy to see. Highcharts® Maps simplifies the creation of interactive, responsive choropleth maps. This post walks through five Highcharts Maps demos, summarized below.
31290: Charts are powerful tools for communicating data, but they can mislead just as easily as they inform. A poorly designed visualization distorts perception, obscures patterns, and undermines decision-making. Understanding common pitfalls helps you create charts that truly serve your audience.
31210: A predictive analytics visualization shows forecast values alongside historical data and confidence intervals, so stakeholders can judge both the prediction and its uncertainty. In Highcharts, you separate history from forecast with zones (for example, solid versus dotted lines), mark the transition with a plot line, and show uncertainty with shaded range bands.
25917: To map the top 100 US cities with Highcharts® Maps, combine a tiledwebmap series (OpenStreetMap provider, Web Mercator projection) with a mapbubble series whose points use lat, lon and a z value for population. Bubble size reflects population, and a tooltip shows each city’s name, state abbreviation and population. Tile-based mapping keeps the map fast and scalable, even with large datasets.
25946: Use a line chart to show how a continuous value changes over time, and use a bar chart to compare values across distinct categories. Line charts highlight trends, seasonal patterns and anomalies, while bar charts make rankings, side-by-side comparisons and proportions easy to read. This guide covers the key characteristics and use cases of both, and how to implement them with Highcharts.
26276: A market depth chart plots the cumulative volume of buy orders (bids) and sell orders (asks) at each price level, showing market liquidity and where supply and demand concentrate. In Highcharts, you build one as an area chart with step: 'center', two series (bids and asks) of [price, cumulative volume] points, and a plot line marking the current price. This article explains how depth charts work, what they reveal about market dynamics, and how to implement them.
30105: Users of financial SaaS platforms need instant visibility into their portfolios, risk metrics and financial goals. You can build that kind of analytics dashboard by combining Highcharts Dashboards with the Morningstar connector. The Morningstar Personal Portfolio Dashboard demo uses Highcharts Dashboards for layout, Highcharts Stock for portfolio performance, Highcharts Grid for holdings, and Morningstar connectors for risk scores and goal analysis.
26498: A radar chart (also called a polar or spider chart) plots three or more quantitative variables on axes that start from the same center point. It works best for comparing a few entities across 5-8 related metrics on a shared scale, and can confuse more than it clarifies when used for the wrong data. This guide covers when radar charts work, when to avoid them, and how to build one in Highcharts by loading highcharts-more.js and setting chart.polar to true.
